title: Twilight House / Spacefiction Studio
text:
Twilight House / Spacefiction Studio

Uprooting into the future – The client wanted to move his parents from their ancestral home to a nature-centric, designed one. The program was to fit more rooms for the children and grandchildren, so they could stay comfortably on their visits, which their current home lacked. The more people age, the more they are rooted in their environment, habits, and ways.

title: A Leaf Canopy by the Sea / Studio 10
text:
A Leaf Canopy by the Sea / Studio 10

The project sits on a tree-lined grassy slope along the coast of Shenzhen Bay Park, one of the city's most popular public parks. The site boasts abundant wildlife and serves as a resting ground for Siberian migratory birds flying south. Centered on a "light intervention" design philosophy, the scheme strikes a subtle balance between public space, park-based retail and ecological conservation.

title: Abejas Sports and Recreation Center / border arquitectos
text:
Abejas Sports and Recreation Center / border arquitectos

The Abejas Sports and Recreation Center in Tijuana explores the role architecture can play in improving everyday life in underserved areas. Developed within a neighborhood shaped by rapid urban growth and limited access to quality public infrastructure, the project introduces a space dedicated to sports, recreation, and community activity.

title: House in Santana do Parnaíba / GRUPOSP
text:
House in Santana do Parnaíba / GRUPOSP

Located in Santana do Parnaíba, this residence establishes an intentional dialogue with the landscape, orienting itself to take advantage of the privileged view of the woods in the adjacent valley, which is fully integrated into its living areas.

title: HUB UCC. Universidad Católica de Córdoba Innovation Space / BLT Arquitectos
text:
HUB UCC. Universidad Católica de Córdoba Innovation Space / BLT Arquitectos

The Universidad Católica de Córdoba operates on a campus that, following the traditional format, originally assigned a building to each academic unit or field of study. In a contemporary world that demands interdisciplinary research and design dynamics, architecture must transcend fragmentation to enhance collective life and foster social cohesion within the academic community. This requires more flexible spaces that, rather than functioning as isolated compartments, encourage the intersection of disciplines and ideas to foster innovation and the development of new projects. The architecture of the hub makes room for what is yet unknown, for innovation, creation, and the materialization of ideas, and for the interdisciplinary convergence of the university community.

title: House on the Northern Coast of Sao Paulo  / André Vainer Arquitetos
text:
House on the Northern Coast of Sao Paulo / André Vainer Arquitetos

Designed for six siblings and their families, this spacious seafront house occupies a corner lot in a housing development tract designed by the brilliant Lúcio Costa. The generous scale of the house called for an L-shaped layout, which allows most of the rooms to face both the sea and the pool and garden enclosed within the site. A separate caretaker’s house is located near the street entrance. Built on a previously filled site, the house stretches in a long, linear form between the required setbacks imposed by local building regulations.

title: 90/100 Mixed Use Project / 5468796 Architecture
text:
90/100 Mixed Use Project / 5468796 Architecture

On a long parcel at the edge of Winnipeg's East Exchange District, 90/100, named for its address, unites a 1905 warehouse with a seven-storey contemporary volume to create a medium-density, mixed-use development. Containing 206 residential suites spanning new and old buildings and 6000 square feet of commercial space, the project establishes a deliberate counterpoint to the area's conventional, opaque residential buildings through careful choreography of massing, open space and glazing, rendering the building physically and symbolically open. It strikes a rare balance contributing to the urban fabric, establishing a landmark distinguished by bold geometry and material precision.

The construction of the new pavilion is part of a larger urban project to reclaim and enhance a large green space called PARCOBROLO, which extends to the southern part of the town of Bonate Sotto in the Villa district, covering an area of over 30,000 square meters. This large orchard (brolo) has survived over time, untouched by the expansion of the surrounding buildings.

title: Public Interest Design in South Africa
text:
Public Interest Design in South Africa

This book presents salient examples of architectural projects and practices in South Africa since 1994 that collectively subscribe to the paradigm shift towards Public Interest Design. Despite radical political transformation in the country, the people of South Africa remain adversely affected by the socio-spatial legacies of a segregated urban landscape. The contributions by architects to address these challenges go largely unnoticed and remain a marginalised practice, even within the mainstream profession.

title: Metaxis: A Collection of Ideas and Objects by FUTUREFORMS
text:
Metaxis: A Collection of Ideas and Objects by FUTUREFORMS

This exhibition takes as its point of departure the Greek word metaxi, referring to an in‑between condition—belonging to two realms at once. METAXIS explores what happens in between: between ideas, objects, spaces, and ways of seeing. It reflects on the dynamic state of being in the middle of things, a shifting tension or oscillation rather than a fixed condition. The exhibited projects move fluidly between perception and imagination, inside and outside, presence and absence, art and architecture. What does it mean to create public art and architecture in the 21st century?

title: Cinema Studio Namibe: Reviving a Tropical Modernist Icon in Angola
text:
Cinema Studio Namibe: Reviving a Tropical Modernist Icon in Angola

What sustains the purpose of architecture that has never been occupied? For decades, this was the question surrounding the Namibe Cinema-Studio, built on the coast of Angola in 1973. Conceived as a film screening venue, the building remained closed and abandoned, never fulfilling the role for which it was created. Yet it withstood the passage of time, becoming an icon of the Angolan landscape and architecture, until finally screening its first film nearly fifty years later.

title: The House of Memories / Studio Lagom
text:
The House of Memories / Studio Lagom

The House of Memories is born from the desire to move ahead with the times and satisfy dynamic requirements, while enshrining familial memories and celebrating its roots. It is located on a 165' x 55' plot in Valsad, a city filled with beautiful farmland and lotus ponds that make a beautiful inclusion in this narrative too, celebrating the context. The home occupies the place of the family's earlier abode, a rambling 22-room structure, which also functioned as their office, standing next to a small well. The client had purchased it from a Parsi gentleman, complete with beautiful wooden furniture. While the rooms were numerous, they were tiny, and the spatial orchestration was not at all user-friendly. Plus, with ageing family members, particularly one who is physically challenged as well, the need to shift to a modern home with an inclusive, barrier-free design became crucial and pressing.

title: Les Feixes Becomes the Setting for a Film Exploring Architecture and Geometry
text:
Les Feixes Becomes the Setting for a Film Exploring Architecture and Geometry

On Spain's Costa Brava, the little-known brutalist housing block Les Feixes, in L'Estartit, becomes the main stage of "Caçador de Geometries" (Geometry Hunter), a short film produced by Simon and directed by filmmaker Matilda Vidal de Llobatera. Its premiere marks the launch of the sixth edition of the Living Places – Simon Architecture Prize, the only award that uses video to explain architecture from the perspective of those who inhabit it. Curated by Fundació Mies van der Rohe since 2016, it is now open and, coinciding with its tenth anniversary, it joins the program of Barcelona 2026, World Capital of Architecture.

title: Oslo Architecture Triennale 2026 Announces Programme for 9th Edition Under "What if Nature Comes First?"
text:
Oslo Architecture Triennale 2026 Announces Programme for 9th Edition Under "What if Nature Comes First?"

The 2026 Oslo Architecture Triennale will take place from September 17 to October 1 at Sofienberg Church in Oslo, bringing together more than 30 international architecture projects around the question "What if Nature Comes First?" For its ninth edition, the Triennale will adopt a two-week festival format, combining an exhibition with conferences, seminars, workshops, film screenings and guided walks. Curated by Line Ramstad, the programme will examine how placing nature at the starting point of architectural decision-making could influence what is built, preserved, transformed or left untouched.

title: Salle de médiation culturelle / atelier iso architectes
text:
Salle de médiation culturelle / atelier iso architectes

The building is located within the Moulin des Gourmands, a tourist site dedicated to the discovery and promotion of traditional milling heritage. Operated by the local tourist office, the site welcomes a wide range of visitors throughout the year, including school groups, individual visitors, associations, and organized groups.

title: Reused Brick and Timber Shape Reiulf Ramstad Arkitekter's New Railway Station in Sweden
text:
Reused Brick and Timber Shape Reiulf Ramstad Arkitekter's New Railway Station in Sweden

Construction is advancing on Gothenburg Grand Central, a new station building and prominent western entrance designed by Reiulf Ramstad Arkitekter. The project is part of the West Link (Västlänken) commuter rail project at Gothenburg Central Station, consisting of 8 kilometers of railway, including three new stations: Centralen, Haga, and Korsvägen. The new route is projected to increase capacity during peak hours and reduce travel times for commuter and regional trains, connecting directly to the existing central station and the Nils Ericson Terminal. The new station is scheduled to open alongside Västlänken's Centralen underground station in December 2026, with office tenants moving in during 2027, and the rest of the tunnel planned to be ready for traffic by December 2030.

title: Ephemeral Architecture Prototypes: The Future of Public Spaces
text:
Ephemeral Architecture Prototypes: The Future of Public Spaces

Concéntrico returned to Logroño for its 12th edition in June 2026, transforming the city into a working site for architecture. Since its founding in 2015, the festival has built an identity on resisting a distant, controlled exhibition of design by constructing full-scale installations in the city's streets, plazas, and vacant lots. Concéntrico embeds installations directly into daily life, engaging residents and visitors as active, observant participants. This year's program brought together more than twenty projects by architects, designers, and researchers working across geographies and methods, each contributing to a citywide experiment in reimagining public space.

title: Tomi House / The Studio
text:
Tomi House / The Studio

Tomi House is built on a 4 × 15.5-meter plot within an existing residential neighborhood in Quy Nhon, Vietnam. Shaped by the constraints of a narrow and deep townhouse, the project brings natural light, ventilation, and everyday family life into the center of the house through its spatial organization.

title: DR House / ARC Architects
text:
DR House / ARC Architects

Located on the north-eastern outskirts of Tashkent, the house sits between two contrasting environments. The site is accessible from two streets, with a canal and gardens on one side and a low-rise residential neighborhood, or mahalla, on the other. The house was positioned to open toward the gardens, while the upper floors offered views of the surrounding landscape and, on clear days, the mountains beyond.

title: Ouse Fashion Lobby / say architects
text:
Ouse Fashion Lobby / say architects

Ouse Fashion is rooted in Hangzhou, with two decades dedicated to one craft: tailoring the warmth of life into clothing. For them, fashion is not merely about appearance — it is about the ease with which one inhabits their daily life. A corporate lobby is the first point of contact between people and a brand. Employees walk in every day and need to feel a sense of purpose in their work. First-time visitors — the materials, the light, the scale — already speak of the brand's taste and standards. Partners step in, and the lobby should emit a signal of an entire aesthetic system.
